title: I can't open powertoys settings by double clicking
author: Septemberlemon
summary: On Windows 10, Settings exits immediately when launched from the PowerToys icon; the reporter attributes the failure to an older Windows CET compatibility problem and reports that disabling CET for the executable or updating Windows resolves it.

judgment.rationale: The new comment provides a specific runtime exception and a credible OS-level hypothesis, but it does not identify the affected Windows 10 build or independently establish that current Windows servicing resolves the crash. That distinction determines whether this is an external platform prerequisite or a PowerToys compatibility defect.
evidence: The affected build is PowerToysUserSetup-0.101.2432.0-x64 on Windows 10, while the reporter says the same action works on Windows 11.
The reporter now reports an immediate PowerToys.Settings.exe Application Error with exception code 0x80131506 (COR_E_EXECUTIONENGINE) in KERNELBASE.dll and says no PowerToys logs are produced.
The reporter says disabling Hardware-enforced Stack Protection for PowerToys.Settings.exe or installing current Windows updates makes Settings open.
No assignee, linked fix, or related confirmed repository change is present; issue #50359 only cross-references this issue as the source of the workaround.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the exact Windows 10 build and servicing state plus the outcome after current cumulative updates before deciding whether any PowerToys-side compatibility work is justified.

fix_assessment.rationale: The available evidence points to a Windows/.NET CET compatibility condition rather than a confirmed PowerToys code path. A PowerToys code change is not supportable until the precise OS servicing boundary and current-update behavior are established.

issue_context.summary: Settings fails before PowerToys logging begins on one Windows 10 machine, and the reporter has found an executable-level CET workaround and reports success after Windows updates.
known_information: The reported failure affects PowerToysUserSetup-0.101.2432.0-x64 installed from GitHub on Windows 10.
Event Viewer reportedly records COR_E_EXECUTIONENGINE (0x80131506) for PowerToys.Settings.exe in KERNELBASE.dll.
The reporter says the app starts after disabling Hardware-enforced Stack Protection for PowerToys.Settings.exe.
The reporter also says newer Windows cumulative updates resolve the condition.
No current linked PR, assignee, or confirmed duplicate covers this issue.
inferences: The crash may occur in .NET runtime initialization before PowerToys application code executes.
If the condition is limited to unsupported or unserviced Windows 10 builds, a PowerToys source fix may not be applicable.
issue_context.analysis: The reporter's new diagnosis is useful and makes a generic diagnostic request inappropriate. The remaining evidence gap is narrow: the exact Windows servicing boundary and a confirmation that current supported servicing resolves the issue.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live issue body, all three comments, labels, assignees, and timeline.
Checked related Settings reports using the reported exception and CET terms; no linked current PowerToys fix was identified.
Checked the cross-reference from issue #50359 and found it uses this report's workaround rather than documenting a common implementation failure.

information_gaps.information: The exact Windows 10 version, OS build, and installed cumulative-update level on the affected machine.
information_gaps.why_needed: Identifies whether the reported CET failure maps to an outdated Windows servicing boundary.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Run winver and provide the full version and OS build, then list whether the latest applicable Windows Update cumulative update is installed.

information_gaps.information: Whether Settings still crashes after fully applying current Windows 10 updates without the PowerToys.Settings.exe CET override.
information_gaps.why_needed: Separates an external operating-system prerequisite from a continuing PowerToys compatibility defect.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Remove the per-program Hardware-enforced Stack Protection override, install all applicable Windows updates, reboot, and launch Settings from the PowerToys icon.

actions.label: Request Windows servicing details

comment.body: Thanks for documenting the immediate `COR_E_EXECUTIONENGINE` crash and the CET workaround. To determine whether this is limited to an older Windows 10 servicing level or still needs a PowerToys compatibility investigation, please provide the exact Windows version and OS build from `winver`, and confirm whether the latest applicable cumulative update is installed. Then, after applying all available updates and rebooting, remove the per-program Hardware-enforced Stack Protection override for `PowerToys.Settings.exe` and report whether Settings still crashes when launched from the PowerToys icon.
